simple.meaning: אֲחַשְׁתָּרָן (ʼăchashtârân) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a mule.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Esther 8:10. The surrounding context includes commandment, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲחַשְׁתָּרָן (H327) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אֲחַשְׁתָּרָן (ʼăchashtârân) / H327 is traced through Esther 8:10, Esther 8:14 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H327. achashteran [ אֲחַשְׁתְּרָן ] adjective (?) royal (from Persian Khshatra , lordship, realm , see Spieg l. with 215) plural הָאֲחַשְׁתְּרָנִים agreeing with הָרֶכֶשׁ Est 8:10 , 14 . אַחַת see אֶחָד . אַט see אטט . below אטד (meaning dubious; perhaps compare Arabic make firm, strong , compare Thes MV).
